title: Track field path components structurally from frame stack, not by re-deriving from flattened path string
context: Kubernetes label keys legitimately contain dots (e.g., `app.kubernetes.io/instance`), which are indistinguishable from path nesting once folded into a dot-joined string. Trying to recover the original structure by slicing/counting dots in the joined path was unreliable, causing silent extraction failures and false-positive reference edges. Touches invariant(s): con_039cee7367 (Memory hygiene is the agent's job, done without waiting for the human: accept shipped roadmap proposals, settle provenance-repair escalations (apply the true commit or drop), re-anchor or stale findings, and land the resulting capture commits through a PR. Only decisions that need genuine product judgment are queued for the human.).
decision: Added `parentPath` and `key` fields to `FieldPathEntry`, computed structurally from the parser's frame stack at build time. Matching now uses exact `parentPath` comparison instead of deriving keys from the flattened path by string manipulation.
consequences: Dotted label keys like `app.kubernetes.io/instance` now round-trip correctly instead of being silently dropped
Mixed selector/label pairs with differing dotted values (prod vs staging) are now correctly rejected for matching instead of collapsing to a false positive
All-dotted selectors (the `helm create` default convention) are now extracted instead of returning null
Frame stack becomes the authoritative source of path structure; the joined string is a derived display form only
alternatives_rejected: Trying to reverse-engineer keys by counting dots in the joined path — fundamentally unreliable when dots appear in both nesting and label keys
Using a different delimiter for path joining — same problem resurfaces with arbitrary label key content
Adding heuristic detection of 'real' vs 'label' dots — adds false-positive/negative risk without solving the underlying ambiguity
